newsletter.subject: Short walks, lower blood pressure
newsletter.text:
A trial run by Kestrel University followed 2,300 adults with mildly high blood pressure for a year.

Those asked to take a 20-minute walk after dinner saw their systolic blood pressure fall by an average of 6 points, compared with 2 points in the group that did not change their routine. The researchers said the effect was about half that of a typical first-line medication.

The study did not include people already on blood pressure medication. The researchers plan a larger trial with 10,000 people next year.

As always, talk to your doctor before changing anything.
